sources.title: Francis J. Narcowich, Joseph D. Ward, and Holger Wendland, Sobolev Bounds on Functions with Scattered Zeros, with Applications to Radial Basis Function Surface Fitting, Mathematics of Computation 74(250) (2005), 743–763
sources.locator: Author-uploaded full text inspected (ResearchGate reader exposes 2,969 lines; uploader is Holger Wendland). Read the complete argument in Theorem 1.1 and §§2.1–2.2, especially the local domain and scattered-zeros reasoning for Theorem 2.12, plus §3.1.1, Lemma 3.1 and Proposition 3.2. The paper's intrinsic W_p fractional-norm/extension route was compared with the local restriction-quotient Fourier proof; no extension theorem is imported.

contents.name: §1, Theorem 1.1: general W_p^(k+s) scattered-zero Sobolev bound on a uniform-cone Lipschitz domain
contents.reason: The selected p=2, zero-order estimate is proved locally for the declared Fourier restriction-quotient H^s norm; the broader source theorem is not used as a supplier.

contents.name: §2.1, Proposition 2.1 and the star-shaped-domain approximation construction
contents.reason: The local proof constructs stable polynomial norming stencils from the admitted cone condition and does not rely on the paper's star-shaped-domain cover or its constants.

contents.name: §2.1.4–§2.2.1, Theorem 2.12: scattered-zero estimates and the uniform-cone domain passage
contents.reason: The item contains a complete independent Fourier high/low-frequency proof for the exact H^(ν+d/2) quotient norm; the source result is comparison context, not a logical premise.

contents.name: §2.2.2, Theorem 2.13: discrete derivative estimates with a mesh-ratio factor
contents.reason: The selected fill-distance interpolation theorem does not require a mesh-ratio assumption, and no discrete derivative estimate from Theorem 2.13 is claimed.

contents.name: §3.1.1, positive-definite RBF Fourier native norm and Lemma 3.1 native-space norm control
contents.reason: The local proof derives the Matérn weighted norm, reproducing property and restricted quotient directly; it does not use the source's extension-operator proof.

contents.reason: The authored theorem proves the selected native Matérn rate through its own projection, quotient-equivalence and zeros-lemma suppliers rather than assuming Proposition 3.2.

contents.name: §3.1.2, Lemma 3.4 and Beppo–Levi/thin-plate spline extension argument
contents.reason: Thin-plate splines and their Beppo–Levi native spaces are outside the selected Matérn and exact augmented-system claims.

alternatives.argument: The carrier proves the exact restriction-quotient H^(nu+d/2) zero bound locally: it constructs stable polynomial norming stencils from the uniform cone condition and gives the Fourier low/high-frequency estimate for functions vanishing on the sites. The source theorem is not used as a premise.

The carrier constructs the finite kernel-span inner product and completion, identifies the Matérn norm by its locally proved positive spectral density, and proves the reproducing identity and strict Gram positivity from Fourier uniqueness/density. It does not import the paper’s extension-operator argument.

The carrier combines its native-space projection theorem, local restricted native/Sobolev identification, and local scattered-zeros bound: the interpolation residual vanishes at sites and has controlled Sobolev norm, giving the h^nu pointwise error bound. It does not assume Proposition 3.2.
